scenario.name: r-obs-cont-provenance
scenario.description: Accepted continuation entry spans carry primitive/origin classification plus stable public-safe run, session, and turn correlation, so a typed-tool span and its accepted-entry span can be causally joined after the fact.
scenario.notes: Construct-only. The continuation telemetry census (karmaterminal/openclaw#1254) established that continuation.work and continuation.delegate.dispatch carry no signal.kind and no session/turn/run identity on the exact product basis 6b09b1db. Until OpenClaw emits the declared attributes there is nothing for a scenario to assert, so this row publishes the contract instead of a scenario.
scenario.registryNotes: Cross-cutting instrumentation contract. It is not a behavioral row: R-CW-1, R-CW-3, R-CD-2, R-CD-4, R-CD-CHAINED-DEPTH-2, R-CD-TOKEN, R-CD-MODEL-TOOL and R-RC-2 each depend on it for their telemetry rebind claim and none of them can honestly own it alone.

census.limits: Accepted entry spans totalled 23 in 24h and 366 in 7d and carried no signal.kind. Primitive attribution came from three separate, non-additive evidence streams (typed-tool spans, bracket effective-signal logs, tool-call effective-signal logs); census confidence for primitive attribution and unique user-visible turns was explicitly low.

spans.name: continuation.work
spans.notes: Exists on 6b09b1db but carries no origin/session/turn/run identity.

spans.name: continuation.delegate.dispatch
spans.notes: Exists on 6b09b1db but carries no origin/session/turn/run identity.

spans.name: openclaw.tool.execution
spans.notes: Typed-tool evidence stream. It cannot currently be joined to an accepted-entry span because neither side shares a stable correlation key.

attributes.notes: Closed enum: typed-tool | tool-call | bracket | post-compaction | queue-drain. Today signal.kind is attached only to continuation.disabled and compaction-release spans.
work | delegate | compaction, on the accepted-entry span rather than only on disabled/compaction-release spans.
Tempo intentionally drops raw session identifiers from exported span attributes; the remedy is a stable salted fingerprint, not the raw key.
No exported span retains a stable turn identifier today, so unique user-visible turns cannot be counted.
Already present on continuation spans and already asserted by the trace-correlation resolvers.

redaction.rule: Identity is published as a salted fingerprint or a closed enum only. Raw session keys, raw run/turn identifiers, prompt or reason bodies, task text, channel payloads and Discord receipt identifiers never enter a span attribute or a committed artifact.
redaction.saltSource: Per-fleet salt supplied at runtime and never committed; fingerprints are stable within a fleet and non-reversible outside it.

controls.positive: In one bounded window fire the same primitive on both entry surfaces: a typed continue_work tool call and a bare CONTINUE_WORK response token. Both must produce accepted-entry spans, the typed one must join to its openclaw.tool.execution span through the shared run fingerprint, and the two spans must report different continuation.signal.origin values while sharing the session fingerprint.
controls.negative: An empty continuation.queue.drain, an unrelated openclaw.run, and a CONTINUE_WORK string carried inside a message tool body must produce no accepted-entry span and no origin attribute. A window with no continuation activity must return zero accepted-entry spans with a complete backend receipt, proving the query itself is not the thing producing the zero.
controls.notes: The negative control is what separates 'no continuation happened' from 'the query or the backend hid it'; the census could not make that separation.

backendUnavailable.notes: During the census, identical historical Tempo searches later returned HTTP 200 live-store-only responses with no totalBlocks and zero historical matches while /ready stayed 200. A response missing the completeness keys is unavailable/partial evidence, never a zero.

artifact.notes: continuation-provenance-receipt.json enumerates every accepted-entry span in the window with its origin enum, identity fingerprints, and the tool span it joined to (or the explicit reason no tool span exists for a bracket origin).

verdictAuthority.pass: Every accepted-entry span in the bounded window carries continuation.signal.origin, continuation.signal.kind and all three identity fingerprints; every typed-tool origin joins to exactly one openclaw.tool.execution span; both positive-control surfaces are distinguishable; the negative controls stay empty; and the backend receipt is complete.
verdictAuthority.partial: The backend receipt is missing a completeness key, the window is degraded/partial, or one or more declared attributes are absent. Absent attributes are recorded as instrumentation debt against karmaterminal/openclaw#1254, never as a behavioral finding.
verdictAuthority.fail: An accepted-entry span reports an origin contradicted by the fired surface, two distinct sessions or turns collide on one fingerprint, or a typed-tool origin joins to more than one tool execution.

execution.deterministicK6: A deterministic k6 row fires both entry surfaces with a runner-owned nonce and a bounded window, then asserts the declared attributes on the exported spans.
execution.manual: Until the product emits the attributes, only the manual Tempo JSON read exists, and it can report nothing but their absence.
execution.relationship: The manual read is the interim instrument and produces PARTIAL only. The deterministic k6 row becomes the authority the moment the product emits the attributes; the manual read then degrades to a spot-check and never overrides the k6 receipt.

expectedReceipts.name: entry-span-origin-attribute
expectedReceipts.description: Every accepted continuation entry span in the bounded window carries continuation.signal.origin and continuation.signal.kind from the closed enum

expectedReceipts.name: entry-span-identity-attributes
expectedReceipts.description: Every accepted entry span carries stable public-safe run, session, and turn fingerprints

expectedReceipts.name: tool-to-entry-causal-join
expectedReceipts.description: Each typed-tool origin joins to exactly one openclaw.tool.execution span through the shared run fingerprint, and each bracket origin proves the absence of a typed-tool span

expectedReceipts.name: both-forms-origin-discrimination
expectedReceipts.description: The typed-tool and token/bracket positive controls fired in one window are separable by origin enum alone

expectedReceipts.name: negative-control-empty
expectedReceipts.description: Empty queue drains, unrelated runs, and message-tool-body tokens produce no accepted-entry span and no origin attribute

expectedReceipts.name: backend-completeness-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: Telemetry backend response carries the declared completeness keys; a degraded response is recorded as unavailable/partial and never as zero

expectedReceipts.name: tempo-trace-json
expectedReceipts.description: Public-safe Tempo trace projection for the bounded window

review.notes: Construct-only remedy contract from the continuation telemetry census. It publishes what OpenClaw must emit before any continuation row can claim a telemetry-rebindable PASS. It must not be read as evidence that the instrumentation exists.

liveRunSafety.notes: Construct-only rows are rejected by the live-run guard. Publication path for a future product PR that lands the instrumentation is PR-NNNNNN/PROOFS/<FULL_SHA>/.
